years.title: First waterworks
years.blurb: The first public waterworks on the Windmühlenberg opened on 1 January 1856: a machine and boiler house, a standpipe tower and a reservoir. The big tower does not exist yet.

years.title: Big tower finished
years.blurb: The big tower was built from 1875 to 1877. The city had bought the plant in 1874. The hill now carries the tower, the machine house and the buried reservoirs.

years.title: SA early camp
years.blurb: In spring 1933 the SA ran an early camp in the cellars of Maschinenhaus I, until about mid-June. The waterworks machines had been shut down in 1914.

years.label: Today
years.title: Park, flats, art
years.blurb: The machine house was blown up in June 1935 and the park opened on 1 May 1937. Today the hill has a park with a playground, a memorial wall, flats in the tower and art in the reservoirs since 1994.

layers.name: Large reservoir
layers.built: Part of the complex dated 1852 to 1877
layers.what: A buried clean-water reservoir under the hill, built as ring-shaped nested barrel vaults.
layers.today: Used for art since 1994: the KrypTonale sound and light festival, concerts and exhibitions, coordinated by Förderband e.V. for the Bezirksamt Pankow. You can only get inside during events or exhibitions; I found no regular opening hours. visitBerlin lists an echo of about 18 seconds, so wear warm clothes.

1856.note: The complex is dated 1852 to 1877 and I found no year for this reservoir, so I show it from 1877.

1877.note: Drawn as part of the finished plant. The city later added a second machine house and a second ground reservoir in 1888.

1933.note: Water use ended in 1914. The vaults then served other purposes until the art use began in 1994.

today.note: Still there, now an event and exhibition space.

layers.name: Small reservoir
layers.built: Part of the complex dated 1852 to 1877
layers.what: A second, smaller buried reservoir, listed together with the large one as part of the same ensemble.
layers.today: An art venue at Diedenhofer Straße 20. Galerie Parterre showed an exhibition there from 1 May to 28 June 2026, Tuesday to Sunday, 12:00 to 20:00. I found no current programme, so check before you go; outside exhibitions I found no regular opening hours.

1856.note: The ensemble is dated 1852 to 1877. I did not find the year this smaller reservoir was built, so it is shown as an outline here.

1877.note: Part of the plant around the new tower.

1933.note: No longer used for water. I found no detail on its use in 1933.

layers.name: Cellars of Maschinenhaus I
layers.what: The cellars under the machine house, about 1,000 m² of floor.
layers.today: Maschinenhaus I was blown up in June 1935 and I found no source on what remains underground. There is nothing to visit here. The site above is a children's playground.

1856.note: The machine and boiler house of the first waterworks stood here.

1877.note: Still the original machine house; the city added a second one in 1888.

1933.note: An early SA camp ran in these cellars from spring until about mid-June 1933. The total number of prisoners is unknown; I found no surviving records. A local memorial group has documented the names of 19 of them. The building was then used as an SA home.

today.note: Blown up in June 1935. Shown as an outline only.

layers.name: Park surface and playground
layers.what: The hilltop park around the tower. Entrances, paths, trees and the playground position still follow the 1937 design.
layers.today: Open park with steep steps up from the street, benches and a playground on the site of Maschinenhaus I. It was renovated from 2000 to 2006, with a circular path and a rose slope. I did not find a step-free route, so check before you bring a pram or a wheelchair.

1856.note: The hill was a waterworks site. The first park was laid out from 1915.

1877.note: Still a technical site. The first park was laid out from 1915.

1933.note: An earlier park existed, but the present layout and the playground date from 1937.

today.note: The park has been open since 1937.

layers.name: Memorial wall
layers.what: A red-brick memorial wall beneath the tower, at the corner of Knaackstraße and Kolmarer Straße, remembering the people held in the 1933 camp.
layers.today: It stands in public space, so you can read the plaque at any time. A glass commentary panel unveiled in December 2005 was deliberately destroyed in February 2024, and I did not find whether it has been replaced.

1856.note: No memorial. The camp was still decades away.

1933.note: The first memorial stone came in 1950, the wall in 1981.

layers.name: Standpipe tower of 1856
layers.what: The small riser tower of the first waterworks, about 3.5 m across. The big tower later took over its job.
layers.today: The machines and the standpipe were shut down in 1914. The listed ensemble still names a riser-pipe tower, but I did not confirm what of it you can see from the park today.

1856.note: The only tower on the hill until the big one was built.

1877.note: Now stands beside the new big tower.

today.note: Named in the listing; what is visible today is unconfirmed.

layers.name: Flats under the tank
layers.what: The lower floors of the big tower held workshops, offices and flats.
layers.today: Still lived in. The Bezirksamt Pankow says ten flats beneath the reservoir are occupied after the renovation of 2000. You cannot go in; you see the tower from the park.

1856.note: The first tower on the hill was the small standpipe.

1877.note: Finished in 1877 with workshops, offices and flats.

1933.note: The residential floors stayed in use when the tower was taken out of service as a water tower in 1952.

layers.name: Tank floor and roof
layers.what: The water tank on top of the tower, under a flat conical roof. Water was stored up here to keep pressure in the pipes. Locals call the tower Dicker Hermann.
layers.today: The tower was taken out of service in May 1952. I found no public access to the tank floor; you see it from outside. The whole ensemble is a listed monument.

1856.note: The big tower was still two decades away.

1877.note: Newly finished, with the tank above the flats.

1933.note: Since 1914 the tank only served as a pressure indicator, until 1952.
